    3. Deep Dive: Creating FREM Models

    3-deep-dive-createFREMmodel.Rmd

    Introduction

    The Full Random Effects Model (FREM) methodology requires a specific restructuring of both the NONMEM control stream and the underlying dataset. Continuous and categorical covariates must be converted into dummy “observations” so their variability and correlation can be estimated alongside the structural parameters via a unified covariance matrix.

    The createFREMmodel() function is the core engine of the PMXFrem package. It automates this complex transformation, taking a standard base model and its dataset and returning a fully configured FREM model ready for execution in NONMEM.

    How createFREMmodel Works Under the Hood

    Rather than trying to inject every covariate simultaneously, createFREMmodel() uses a robust iterative strategy. First, it bootstraps a “minimal” FREM model using only the first covariate listed in your covariates argument. It completely rewrites the $INPUT, $DATA, $PK, and $ERROR blocks to support the FREM architecture for this single covariate. Then, it iterates through the remaining covariates, utilizing updateFREMmodel() in the background to safely and seamlessly fold each subsequent covariate into the expanding OMEGA block and dataset.

    1. Setup and Paths

    First, load the package and define the paths to your base model and original clinical dataset.

    Note: By default, createFREMmodel writes the final files to the modDevDir directory. It has built-in overwrite protection and will throw an error if files with your fremModName already exist. For this vignette, we will generate a unique temporary directory to safely store the output.

    library(PMXFrem)

# Define paths to example data and converged models
modDevDir <- system.file("extdata", "SimNeb", package = "PMXFrem")
ffemDataFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimNeb/DAT-2-MI-PMX-2-onlyTYPE2-new.csv", package = "PMXFrem")

# Create a temporary directory for all generated outputs
td <- tempdir()

    2. Designing the FREM Model

    We need to decide which covariates to include and how they should be handled. In FREM, continuous covariates can be modeled as-is or log-transformed, while categorical covariates must be identified so they can be binarized into dummy variables.

    We will also explicitly define keep_cols to ensure that critical variables from our base dataset carry over correctly to the new FREM dataset rows.

    # Define the complete list of covariates to include
frem_covariates <- c("AGE", "WT", "SEX", "RACEL")

# Identify categorical and log-transformed covariates
categorical_covs <- c("RACEL", "SEX")
log_transform_covs <- c("WT")

# Define which structural columns must be kept in the new FREM dataset rows
keep_cols <- c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "EVID", "RATE", "FOOD", "DV")

    3. Generating the Model

    We pass our specifications into createFREMmodel(). We use the run30 base model, which has 7 structural THETAs (numNonFREMThetas) and 2 specific OMEGAs that we want to skip correlating with the covariates (numSkipOm).

    Handling Dichotomous Covariates (bRecodeDichotomous): Notice that we set bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE. In many standard datasets, dichotomous variables are coded as 1 and 2 (e.g., Males = 1, Females = 2). If left as-is, the intercept of the FREM covariate effect becomes harder to interpret. When this argument is TRUE, the function automatically detects 2-level categorical covariates and recodes them to 0 and 1. This cleanly establishes the 0 level as the reference baseline.

    # Execute the creation of the FREM model and dataset
generated_files <- createFREMmodel(
  modName            = "run30",
  modDevDir          = modDevDir,
  ffemDataFile       = ffemDataFile,
  outputDir          = td,
  fremModName       = "run30_FREM",
  
  # Covariate Instructions
  covariates         = frem_covariates,
  catCovs            = categorical_covs,
  logtCovs           = log_transform_covs,
  
  # Structural Architecture
  numNonFREMThetas   = 7,
  numSkipOm          = 2,
  
  # Dataset formatting
  cstrKeepCols       = keep_cols,
  bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE,
  quiet              = TRUE
)

    4. Understanding the Output

    createFREMmodel() has now generated the newly expanded .mod and .csv files. Let’s inspect them directly from the disk.

    The Generated Dataset

    The original dataset has been vertically expanded. For every subject, new rows (EVID = 2) have been appended containing the standardized covariate values in the DV column, mapped via the new FREMTYPE compartment column. Because we used bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE, you will see SEX represented as a clean 0 or 1 dummy variable.

    # Read the generated dataset
frem_data <- read.csv(generated_files$data)

# Display the first 15 rows to show the structural PK data followed by the new FREM dummy rows
head(frem_data, n = 15)
#>    ID TIME AMT EVID RATE FOOD     DV FREMTYPE
#> 1   1  0.0   5    4   -2    0  0.000        0

    The Final Model Control Stream

    The control stream is vastly different. The $PK block now handles the structural ETAs alongside the covariate means, and the $ERROR block dynamically routes the dummy observations (via FREMTYPE) to their respective equations. Finally, a massive $OMEGA BLOCK is appended to estimate the covariances.

    # Read the generated NONMEM control stream and print it in its entirety
frem_mod <- readLines(generated_files$model)
cat(frem_mod, sep = "\n")
;; 1. Based on: 25
;; 2. Description:
;;    New simulated data set
;; 3. Label:
;;    SimVal base model
;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$PROBLEM    run 1
$INPUT ID TIME AMT EVID RATE FOOD DV FREMTYPE
$DATA run30_FREM_data.csv IGNORE=@
$SUBROUTINE ADVAN2 TRANS2
$PK
;;; MATFOOD-DEFINITION START
IF(FOOD.EQ.1) MATFOOD = 1  ; Most common
IF(FOOD.EQ.0) MATFOOD = ( 1 + THETA(6))
;;; MATFOOD-DEFINITION END

;;; MAT-RELATION START
MATCOVTIME = MATFOOD
;;; MAT-RELATION END


;;; FRELFOOD-DEFINITION START
IF(FOOD.EQ.1) FRELFOOD = 1  ; Most common
IF(FOOD.EQ.0) FRELFOOD = ( 1 + THETA(7))
;;; FRELFOOD-DEFINITION END

;;; FREL-RELATION START
FRELCOVTIME = FRELFOOD
;;; FREL-RELATION END

TVFREL  = THETA(1)
TVCL    = THETA(2)
TVV     = THETA(3)
TVMAT   = THETA(4)
TVD1    = THETA(5)

;MU_1  = LOG(TVRUV)
MU_2  = TVD1
MU_3  = LOG(TVCL)
MU_4  = LOG(TVV)
MU_5  = LOG(TVMAT)

D1FR  = MU_2                   + ETA(2)
FREL  = TVFREL*FRELCOVTIME
CL    = EXP(MU_3               + ETA(3))
V     = EXP(MU_4               + ETA(4))
MAT   = MATCOVTIME * EXP(MU_5  + ETA(5))
D1    = MAT*(1-D1FR)

F1    = FREL
KA    = 1 / (MAT-D1)
S2    = V

      MU_6 = THETA(8)
      COV6 = MU_6 + ETA(6)
      MU_7 = THETA(9)
      COV7 = MU_7 + ETA(7)
      MU_8 = THETA(10)
      COV8 = MU_8 + ETA(8)
      MU_9 = THETA(11)
      COV9 = MU_9 + ETA(9)
      MU_10 = THETA(12)
      COV10 = MU_10 + ETA(10)
$ERROR
CP    = A(2)*1000 / V
IPRED = LOG(CP + 0.00001)
Y     = IPRED + EPS(1) * EXP(ETA(1))

;;;FREM CODE BEGIN COMPACT
;;;DO NOT MODIFY
      IF(FREMTYPE.EQ.100) THEN
;        AGE 1
         Y = COV6 + EPS(2)
         IPRED = COV6
      END IF
      IF(FREMTYPE.EQ.200) THEN
;        WT 1
         Y = COV7 + EPS(2)
         IPRED = COV7
      END IF
      IF(FREMTYPE.EQ.300) THEN
;        SEX_2 1
         Y = COV8 + EPS(2)
         IPRED = COV8
      END IF
      IF(FREMTYPE.EQ.400) THEN
;        RACEL_2 1
         Y = COV9 + EPS(2)
         IPRED = COV9
      END IF
      IF(FREMTYPE.EQ.500) THEN
;        RACEL_3 1
         Y = COV10 + EPS(2)
         IPRED = COV10
      END IF
;;;FREM CODE END COMPACT
$THETA 1 FIX ; 1. TVFREL
$THETA 6.17206 ; 2. TVCL
$THETA 121.358 ; 3. TVV
$THETA 1.91756 ; 4. TVMAT
$THETA 0.676682 ; 5. D1
$THETA -0.0521041 ; 6. FRELFOOD1
$THETA 0.152505 ; 7. MATFOOD1
$THETA 43 ; 8 TV_AGE
$THETA 86.800168374817 ; 9 TV_WT
$THETA 0.441095890410959 ; 10 TV_SEX_2
$THETA 0.195369030390738 ; 11 TV_RACEL_2
$THETA 0.0246020260492041 ; 12 TV_RACEL_3
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) 0.054943 ; 1. IIV on RUV
$OMEGA BLOCK(1) 1e-04 FIX ; 2. IIV on D1
$OMEGA BLOCK(8) 
0.183099  ; 3. IIV on CL
0.140718 0.200553  ; 4. IIV on V
0.012395 0.0258711 0.047017  ; 5. IIV on MAT
1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 182.584  ; 6 BSV_AGE
1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 428.13879167982  ; 7 BSV_WT
1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 0.246868481876092  ; 8 BSV_SEX_2
1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 0.157427798401812  ; 9 BSV_RACEL_2
1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 1e-05 0.0240315442857442  ; 10 BSV_RACEL_3
$SIGMA  0.0321471  ;     1. RUV
$SIGMA 0.0000001 FIX
$ESTIMATION METHOD=IMPMAP AUTO=1 RANMETHOD=3P INTER NOABORT PRINT=1
            NOCOV=1 ISAMPEND=100 NITER=50 ISAMPLE=300
$ESTIMATION METHOD=IMPMAP INTER EONLY=1 NITER=50 ISAMPLE=10000 NOCOV=0
;            PHITYPE=1
;$COVARIANCE PRINT=E MATRIX=S UNCONDITIONAL

    You can now submit run30_FREM.mod directly to NONMEM for execution!
